subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 4: Vocabulary and Grammar – Verbs and could / couldn’t
outcomes: I can say verb phrases like post a letter, tie a shoelace and win a race.
I can talk about past ability: When I was one, I could walk, but I couldn't talk.
I can ask and answer: Could you swim when you were five? Yes, I could.

tf.s: Could is the past of can.
tf.why: Yes! We use could for ability in the past.

tf.s: "She could sends an email." is correct.
tf.why: After could, use the base verb: She could send an email.

tf.s: Could is the same for I, you, he, she, we and they.
We say "post an email" and "send a letter" in this lesson.
tf.why: The phrases are post a letter and send an email.

tf.s: "Could you talk when you were two?" "Yes, I could." is correct.
tf.why: Great! Could you …? Yes, I could.

tf.s: We say "win a race" and "tie a shoelace".
tf.why: Yes! These are verb phrases from the lesson.

tf.s: "When I was one, I could talked." is correct.
tf.why: Use the base verb: I could talk.

tf.s: We say "hold a story" and "tell a pen".
tf.why: We say tell a story and hold a pen.

tf.s: The short answer to "Could he swim?" is "No, he didn't."
tf.why: We answer with could: No, he couldn't.

boxes.q: When I was two, I ___ hold a pen.
Could you send an email when you were three?
Rawan couldn't post a letter, ___ she could make a face.

boxes.why: We make a sandwich, and we make a face.

boxes.q: ___ Hazim tell a story when he was three?

mcq.q: Which list has only verb phrases from the lesson?
o: post a letter, tie a shoelace, make a face
carry a bag, call the doctor, study Maths
bake a cake, fix toys, juggle
curly hair, a beard, a moustache
mcq.why: These are this lesson's verb phrases.

o: Could you talk when you were two?
Could you talked when you were two?
Did you could talk when you were two?
Could you talking when you were two?

mcq.q: Which sentence is from the grammar box idea?
o: When I was one, I could walk, but I couldn't talk.
When I was one, I can walk.
When I was one, I could walked.
When I am one, I could walk.
mcq.why: Could and couldn't for past ability.

mcq.q: Make a question: you / tie a shoelace / when you were four
o: Could you tie a shoelace when you were four?
Could you tied a shoelace when you were four?
Can you tie a shoelace when you were four?
You could tie a shoelace when you were four?
mcq.why: Could + you + base verb + when you were …?

mcq.q: Write: Rawan / post a letter (no) / make a face (yes)
o: Rawan couldn't post a letter, but she could make a face.
Rawan could post a letter, but she couldn't make a face.
Rawan couldn't posted a letter, but she could made a face.
Rawan can't post a letter, but she can make a face.

mcq.q: You couldn't swim last year, but you can swim now. Which sentence is correct?
o: I couldn't swim last year, but I can swim now.
I can't swim last year, but I could swim now.
I could swim last year, but I can't now.
mcq.why: couldn't for the past, can for now.

mcq.q: Find the mistake: "She could sends an email."
mcq.why: After could, use the base verb.

mcq.q: A baby is one year old. Which sentence is most likely true?
mcq.why: A one-year-old baby can't use email yet.

mcq.q: Why do we say "he could" and not "he coulds"?
o: Could is the same for all persons.
